title: No pointer check for NULL before it is dereferenced in evp_pkey_asn1_ctrl
body:
OpenSSL 3.0.7

In function evp_pkey_asn1_ctrl, there is no pointer check to NULL before it is dereferenced. This function is used in functions
EVP_PKEY_set1_encoded_public_key, EVP_PKEY_get1_encoded_public_key, EVP_PKEY_get_default_digest_nid. 
Functions EVP_PKEY_set1_encoded_public_key and EVP_PKEY_get1_encoded_public_key are deprecated in OpenSSL 3.0, but function EVP_PKEY_get_default_digest_nid can be used. In EVP_PKEY_get_default_digest_nid (and other depreceted functions) can be passed NULL as the 1st argument, next this NULL pointer is passed as 1st argument in call to function evp_pkey_asn1_ctrl, where it is dereferenced.

Maybe need to add a check EVP_PKEY *pkey to NULL in a function evp_pkey_asn1_ctrl and return -2 if it equal NULL?
author: nv-dmd

comments.body: What about this issuer? Can I make PR?
We do not do similar NULL checks in other similar functions. I am not sure this is really worth it.
Maybe then add a check to NULL the 1st argument in the functions EVP_PKEY_set1_encoded_public_key, EVP_PKEY_get1_encoded_public_key, EVP_PKEY_get_default_digest_nid and return 0 if equal NULL?
That would be okay I think.

Sorry. I missed that this issue has already been fixed in the pull request #20294. 
Close this issue/

satisfaction_conditions: A solution that prevents NULL pointer dereference in the evp_pkey_asn1_ctrl function
Guidance on the appropriate approach for handling NULL pointers in OpenSSL functions
Confirmation that the issue has been addressed in some form

title: Options `-ssl3`,, `-no_ssl3`, `-no_tls1`, `-no_tls1_1`, `-no_tls1_2`, `-no_tls1_3`,  not recognised
body:
_release:_ openssl-3.0.5

_manual reference:_
```
$ man 'OPENSSL(1ossl)'
(...)
       -ssl3, -tls1, -tls1_1, -tls1_2, -tls1_3, -no_ssl3, -no_tls1, -no_tls1_1, -no_tls1_2, -no_tls1_3
           These options require or disable the use of the specified SSL or TLS protocols. (...)
```
Hello. options `-ssl3`,, `-no_ssl3`, `-no_tls1`, `-no_tls1_1`, `-no_tls1_2`, `-no_tls1_3`,  not recognised; illustration:
```
$ openssl ciphers -ssl3
list: Use -help for summary.
```
As opposed, other options are recognised; illustration:
```
$ openssl ciphers -tls1_3 | sed 's/:/\n/g' | head -1
TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
```
author: Ricky-Tigg

comments.body: The no_* options do not apply to the ciphers command but they apply to other commands such as s_client. The -ssl3 option is probably not supported by your build but it is supported if enable-ssl3 is used with the build configuration. So perhaps some clarification in the manual page would be appropriate but the options should not be removed from the manual page.

That was much helpful. At the time the report was sent, i was not yet aware of the existence of `openssl help <command>`. Now I am. Consulting `openssl help ciphers` would have been beneficial before reporting. Then, by default,  version 3 of SSL was disabled which, if i interpret correctly, caused the output.
```
$ openssl list -disabled | column
Disabled algorithms:	MDC2	SM4	EC2M	SM2	SSL3
```

satisfaction_conditions: Clarification on which OpenSSL commands support specific SSL/TLS protocol options
Explanation for why the -ssl3 option specifically wasn't recognized
Information about alternative ways to get command-specific help in OpenSSL

title: const mismatch between
